events.headline: UN Report: Over 1,100 Killed in Haiti Gang Violence in Third Quarter of 2026
events.summary: A UN report (BINUH) found at least 1,167 people killed and 459 injured in Haiti between July and September 2026 amid gang attacks, including massacres. The report documented 344 cases of sexual violence during the period.

events.headline: Brooklyn Building Collapse Death Toll Rises to Eight as Victims Identified
events.summary: The death toll from the Flatbush Avenue building collapse into an adjacent construction excavation rose to eight as FDNY concluded its search, including two children; 17-18 people were injured. Officials say the demolished-but-unremoved building had been ordered razed six months earlier.
events.locationName: Flatbush, Brooklyn, New York, United States

events.headline: Iran Warns It Will 'Rain Down Hell' if US Resumes Strikes Amid Qeshm Island Tensions
events.summary: Iran threatened to retaliate forcefully if the US resumes military strikes, following earlier US action near Qeshm Island. The US has evacuated aircraft from a second UK base as tensions between Washington and Tehran persist.

events.headline: Russia and Ukraine Advance Plans for War's Largest Prisoner Swap After Witkoff-Kushner-Putin Kremlin Meeting
events.summary: Following a Kremlin meeting between US envoys Witkoff and Kushner and Putin, and a follow-up briefing with Zelensky in Dublin, officials floated scale figures as high as 1,500-for-1,500 for what would be the war's largest POW exchange, with no swap yet executed. Kushner said both sides also agreed to bring European partners into the next round of talks.

events.headline: Salvadoran-Backed Forces Kill Up to 20 in Haiti Gang Raid Amid Hunt for Missing Soldiers
events.summary: Following the October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians, El Salvador deployed about 2,500 troops to Haiti. A November 8-9 helicopter and munitions strike destroyed a gang house near Port-au-Prince, killing up to 20 people.

events.headline: TTP Ambush Near Kohat Kills 10 Police and 18 Militants in Gun Battle
events.summary: Gunmen ambushed a police convoy returning from an anti-illegal-mining operation in Gumbat, Kohat district, on November 11-12. Ten police were killed and 12 or more wounded, with two vehicles torched; security forces killed 18 attackers, and the TTP claimed responsibility.

events.headline: Iran Extends IAEA Inspector Blackout as Trump Says US Doesn't Need a Deal
events.summary: A restricted IAEA document said inspectors still cannot verify the location of Iran's near-bomb-grade uranium stockpile, with Iran continuing to block inspectors from key facilities since mid-2025. Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran, with no new talks scheduled despite Qatari mediation, after Iran separately rejected a US proposal to move its enriched uranium stockpile abroad.

events.headline: Myanmar Military Airstrike on Rakhine IDP Camp Kills 12 Civilians Including a Child
events.summary: A Myanmar military jet bombed the Byar La displacement camp near Sittwe in Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine State, on the evening of November 13, killing 12 civilians including a five-year-old and injuring 18 others. The strike came days after a similar deadly airstrike on another IDP site in the same region.

events.headline: Cindy Holscher Confirmed Winner of Closest Kansas Governor's Race in Decades
events.summary: The AP called Kansas's governor's race for Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher over Republican Senate President Ty Masterson on Nov. 12, more than a week after election day, as her lead grew past 7,000 votes. Masterson conceded, giving Democrats a third consecutive gubernatorial win in Kansas, succeeding term-limited Gov. Laura Kelly.

events.headline: Storm Floods 70,000 Tents in Gaza Overnight, Destroying Thousands of Family Shelters
events.summary: A storm flooded roughly 70,000 tents across Gaza in a single night, destroying 6,000 to over 9,000 family shelters and damaging more than 17,400 others across all five governorates; the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis also flooded. Five to six deaths have been linked to the storm and cold, and the UN is calling for 150,000 additional tents to be allowed into the territory.

events.headline: WHO: Global Cholera Deaths Pass 3,000 in 2026, DRC Among Worst-Hit Outbreaks in Decades
events.summary: WHO data shows global cholera deaths topped 3,000 across 28 countries in the first nine months of 2026, with the DRC outbreak among the worst in decades and spreading toward Kinshasa; the DRC's own death toll is disputed between sources, with estimates ranging from about 1,800 to over 3,600.

events.headline: North Carolina Congressional Delegation Flips to 11-3 Democratic After Canvasses
events.summary: Finalized county canvasses show North Carolina Democrats flipped seven U.S. House seats, shifting the state's delegation from 10-4 Republican to 11-3 Democratic. In the 5th District, Democrat Chuck Hubbard's lead over longtime GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx grew to about 335 votes after provisional and cured ballots were counted, though a recount remains possible.

events.headline: Israeli Strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital Kills at Least Eight, Including a Surgeon
events.summary: An Israeli airstrike overnight on November 11-12 hit a surgical ward building at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, killing at least eight people including surgeon Rezik Abushira and wounding about 20. Israel said it targeted a senior Hamas commander; Hamas denies this, and it is the first strike on the hospital since the October 2025 ceasefire.

events.headline: Nvidia Shares Plunge Amid Reports Board Weighs CEO Jensen Huang's Future
events.summary: Nvidia shares fell roughly 8-9% after reports that the company's board is discussing CEO Jensen Huang's position amid allegations including purported ties to Chinese intelligence. The board reportedly discussed contingency plans for an interim CEO.

events.headline: Federal Report Finds Communication Gaps, Extreme Fire Behavior Led to Deaths of 4 Firefighters in Colorado's Knowles Fire
events.summary: A joint federal investigation released Nov. 12 found extraordinary fire behavior, strained communications, incomplete situational awareness and gaps in aerial supervision contributed to the deaths of firefighters Nick Hutcherson, Emily Barker, Sydney Watson and Nathan Matthews on June 27. The fire ran about 7.5 miles in under three hours, with only nine seconds between a radio call that a helicopter could not land and a report that crews had deployed emergency shelters.

events.headline: Haiti Hunger Crisis Deepens: Nearly 6 Million Face Severe Food Insecurity
events.summary: A new IPC analysis finds 5.94 million Haitians face severe food insecurity amid spreading gang violence and high food prices. The World Food Programme says it needs $78 million to sustain operations through March 2027.

events.headline: Ethiopia Imposes Indefinite Nighttime Curfew in Mekelle Amid Tigray-Eritrea Tensions
events.summary: Ethiopian federal forces imposed an indefinite nighttime curfew in Mekelle, capital of the Tigray region, amid escalating fighting near Sheraro against Eritrean-backed "Alliance for Survival" forces following reports of Eritrean troops crossing into northern Ethiopia in October. The US Embassy in Addis Ababa has issued repeated security alerts.

events.headline: Second Child Dies in Wisconsin Measles Outbreak as Cases Near 650
events.summary: Wisconsin health officials confirmed a second measles-associated death of a Grant County child on Nov. 13, weeks after the state's first measles death in 36 years. The outbreak, which began in July, has reached 651 cases across 22 counties, with nine counties newly reporting cases in the past week.

events.headline: Iran Says Gas Tanker Struck Mine and Caught Fire in Strait of Hormuz, Warns of 'Unlimited Response'
events.summary: Iran's IRGC Navy said a liquefied-gas carrier hit a sea mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, warning other vessels of the "same fate"; this adds to an escalating pattern of maritime attacks, with roughly 10 ships reportedly hit in the first ten days of November after 37 in October.
events.locationName: Strait of Hormuz, near Sirik, Iran

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Set Massive Fire at Russia's Ust-Luga Baltic Oil Port, Injure Three
events.summary: Overnight on November 10-11, Ukrainian drones struck Novatek's oil terminal at Ust-Luga port in Leningrad Oblast, causing a large fire visible from Estonia and an oil spill. Three workers were injured at a port that handles about 700,000 barrels per day of Russian petroleum exports.

events.headline: EU Ambassadors Endorse 22nd Russia Sanctions Package Targeting 50 Banks, Shadow Fleet
events.summary: EU ambassadors agreed on November 12 to add 50 Russian banks plus individuals and entities linked to the shadow fleet, energy sector and disinformation to sanctions. The package also targets crypto platforms, with formal adoption by foreign ministers expected November 16.

events.headline: California Supreme Court Sets Nov. 24 Deadline for Briefs on Newsom's Death-Row Commutations
events.summary: The California Supreme Court formally invited amicus briefs from prosecutors, defense groups and victims' families on the legality of Gov. Gavin Newsom's bid to commute all 548 death sentences to life without parole. Briefs are due Nov. 24, with Newsom's consolidated response due Dec. 4; advocacy groups have already filed supporting briefs while prosecutors signal opposition.

events.headline: Alaska US Senate Race: Peltola Extends Lead Over Sullivan Ahead of Ranked-Choice Tabulation
events.summary: With about 245,470 first-choice ballots counted (roughly 84% of expected total), Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan 48.8% to 47.1%, a roughly 4,250-vote margin. Since neither candidate cleared 50%, the race heads to Alaska's official ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18, a contest with national implications for Senate control.

events.headline: Indonesia's Wildfire Haze and Urban Pollution Linked to 5,310 Deaths in September Alone, Study Finds
events.summary: A CREA report found an estimated 5,310 air-pollution-linked deaths in Indonesia in September 2026 alone, a 42% jump from August, with about 58 million people exposed to unhealthy or hazardous air concentrated in Kalimantan and Sumatra.

events.headline: Russian Overnight Missile and Drone Attack Kills One, Injures Several in Kyiv
events.summary: Russia launched a large-scale overnight strike with ballistic missiles and about 123 drones on November 11-12; a drone hit a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, killing a 44-year-old woman and injuring several others, with power outages across multiple regions.

events.headline: FAA Blames Contractor L3Harris for Nationwide Ground Stop as Flight Cancellations Top 9,000
events.summary: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said contractor L3Harris was behind the air traffic control data overload that forced a nationwide FAA ground stop, with the exact cause -- a faulty router or contractor error -- still under investigation. Cancellations topped 9,132 flights on Friday and 5,000-6,000 on Saturday, with the FAA projecting 4,000-5,000 more Sunday before full schedule restoration by Sunday night.

events.headline: Eisenkot Advances Israeli Coalition Talks With Possible Haredi Partners as Netanyahu Fights to Stay Relevant
events.summary: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming Israel's next government, said he remains open to Netanyahu joining a unity coalition while exploring partnership with Haredi parties, though insisting the opposition won't drop conscription demands. The Joint List pledged support.

events.headline: G7 Foreign Ministers Issue Strongest Joint Warning Yet on China's Military Activity Near Taiwan
events.summary: Following a Paris meeting, G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement on November 11-12 calling China's assertive activity in waters east of Taiwan a threat to regional stability and freedom of navigation, described as the strongest unified G7 language to date. Taiwan's Presidential Office welcomed it.

events.headline: Houthis Fire Ballistic Missiles at Aden Camp; Saudi Arabia Intercepts Projectiles Near Mecca Province
events.summary: Yemen's government army accused Houthi forces of firing ballistic missiles at the Ras Abbas camp in Aden on November 13, calling it a 'dangerous escalation.' Saudi Arabia intercepted missiles and drones near Mecca Province, with debris found near Sabuhah village; the Houthis denied targeting Mecca, saying their operations target Saudi oil and military infrastructure.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia's Volgograd Oil Refinery, Killing Four Workers
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil-Volgogradneftepererabotka refinery overnight as part of a wave Russia says involved nearly 1,200 drones; the regional governor confirmed four workers killed and two hospitalized. Ukraine's General Staff said it hit multiple crude-distillation and hydrotreating units, the refinery's 13th such strike since February 2024.

events.headline: EPC Summit in Dublin Holds First-Ever Leaders' Discussion on AI Policy; Tikhanovskaya Urges Pressure on Belarus
events.summary: About 50 European leaders met in Dublin on November 12 for the ninth European Political Community summit. An informal European Council on November 13 held the EU's first strategic discussion on AI policy, while Belarusian opposition leader Tikhanovskaya urged continued sanctions on Lukashenko.

events.headline: Taiwan Tracks Dozens More Chinese Aircraft and Ships as Unannounced PLA Deployment Continues
events.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry tracked 10 PLA aircraft, eight naval vessels and three official ships in the 24 hours to November 14, with four sorties crossing the median line, part of an unannounced deployment of over 100 vessels first reported November 13. Taiwan says it has tracked Chinese aircraft 184 times and ships 141 times so far this month.

events.headline: Trump Says He Would Consider Military Action to 'Get Cuba Done' Before Leaving Office
events.summary: In remarks to radio host Hugh Hewitt, Trump said he wants to resolve the Cuba situation before leaving office in 2029 and, when asked directly, said he would "certainly consider" a short US military campaign against Cuba's government, a more explicit escalation than earlier rhetoric focused on sanctions and the oil blockade.

events.headline: Pakistan Military Says It Killed 74 Militants in 10 Days of Border Operations
events.summary: Pakistan's military said it killed 74 militants over 10 days of operations since November 3 -- 43 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Mir Ali and Orakzai districts and 31 in Balochistan. Separately, security forces killed eight militants including a suicide bomber overnight near Kolpur, Balochistan, in an operation that also saw two soldiers killed in a quadcopter attack.

events.headline: NTSB Finds Learjet Tail Section Separated Before Fatal Florida Crash That Killed 9
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin to the Bahamas crashed near Greenacres, Florida on November 1, killing all nine aboard. Investigators found the left tail elevator separated in flight, found in three pieces up to 3.8 miles from the crash site.

events.headline: Mexico City 'Gen Z' Protest Against Crime and Corruption Turns Violent, Injuring About 120
events.summary: Roughly 17,000 people marched from the Monumento a la Revolución to the Zócalo in Mexico City on November 15 to protest crime, corruption and President Sheinbaum's government. Clashes broke out near the Palacio Nacional, injuring about 120 people, mostly police, and leading to roughly 20 arrests.

events.headline: FARC Dissidents Kill Up to Four Soldiers in Drone Attack Near Colombia-Venezuela Border
events.summary: A drone attack attributed to FARC dissident Frente 33 killed three to four Colombian soldiers and wounded three to five others in Tibú, Norte de Santander, near the Venezuelan border on November 12. The attack, suspected to have been launched from Venezuelan territory, came amid Colombia's seventh round of aerial bombing against the group this year.

events.headline: Two Fishermen Beheaded in Fresh Insurgent Raids Across Mozambique's Cabo Delgado
events.summary: Two fishermen were beheaded in Muidumbe district amid a wave of insurgent raids, abductions and roadblocks reported across Cabo Delgado, part of the same period of violence that IOM says has displaced over 7,000 people from the province since late September. Unconfirmed higher casualty claims circulating separately remain unverified.

events.headline: Congress Remains Without Shutdown Deal One Month Before Dec. 11 Funding Deadline
events.summary: As of November 11, Senate and House appropriators had reached no agreement on government funding ahead of the December 11 deadline. Democrats favor a short-term stopgap while the NDAA, FISA 702 and farm bill also remain pending.

events.headline: Egypt's Central Bank Raises Key Rates to 20%/21% Amid Pound Pressure, First Hike Since March 2024
events.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt raised its deposit rate from 19% to 20% and lending rate from 20% to 21% on November 1, its first hike since March 2024, citing external pressure and pound weakness. The move surprised analysts.

events.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Senior Hamas Commander in Khan Younis as Gaza Toll Mounts
events.summary: An Israeli strike killed Hamas Rafah Brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. Gaza's Health Ministry reported 16 people killed and 68 injured strip-wide over 48 hours, including an infant who died of cold exposure, the 11th such death this winter.

events.headline: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Resigns After Court Rules Diploma Ineligible
events.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on November 12 after courts ruled his overseas high-school diploma did not meet eligibility requirements, becoming the first vice president to resign before the end of his term since the 1998 reforms. Parliament has scheduled a succession vote.

events.headline: Sudanese Army Captures Al-Khuwai and Serif Ankoush, Extending West Kordofan Advance
events.summary: Sudan's army and allied forces captured the towns of Serif Ankoush and Al-Khuwai (El Khuwei) in West Kordofan, their first full locality taken in the state, building on the earlier capture of Iyal Bakhit on Nov 9. The gains open a strategic road toward the RSF's regional stronghold of En Nahud.

events.headline: Trump Threatens to Double Tariffs on Mexico Over Migrant Caravan
events.summary: A November 12 Truth Social post threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops a caravan of roughly 1,500 migrants that departed Tapachula; President Sheinbaum disputed Trump's characterization of events.

events.headline: Tanzanian Court Clears Opposition Leader Tundu Lissu of Treason, Jails Him Four Years for Incitement
events.summary: Tanzania's High Court cleared CHADEMA opposition leader Tundu Lissu of a treason charge that had carried a potential death penalty, but convicted him of incitement and sentenced him to four years in prison over alleged calls to "block the election." Rights groups call the case politically motivated; Lissu plans to appeal.

events.headline: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race, First Black Senator From State Since 1874
events.summary: AP called Mississippi's Senate race for Scott Colom over incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith on November 11. Colom is the first Black senator from Mississippi since 1874 and the eighth Senate seat Democrats have flipped in the 2026 midterms.

events.headline: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Top 5,400, Highest Since 1991
events.summary: The United States recorded more than 5,400 measles cases and 10 deaths in 2026, losing its measles elimination status after holding it for 26 years. The Pan American Health Organization reported a regional surge of 57,666 cases and 81 deaths across the Americas, including 53 in Guatemala, 23 in Mexico and three in the US.

events.headline: FRN Rebel Fighting Kills Over 10 Civilians in DRC's South Kivu as Doha Talks Falter
events.summary: Clashes involving the Kabila-aligned FRN rebel coalition killed more than 10 civilians over a week of fighting since November 6 in the Kalima grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu. The violence comes as the FRN threatens to quit Doha peace talks over a planned constitutional referendum.

events.headline: Global Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Hospitals, Government Agencies and Transit Worldwide
events.summary: A worldwide Microsoft 365 outage centered on Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Copilot hit November 12-13, triggering a 'Code Grey' at a Toronto hospital network, disrupting Via Rail notifications, and affecting Australian government agencies including the AFP and ASIO. Microsoft cited elevated load across multiple regions.

events.headline: Pacific Storm Triggers Coastal Evacuation Warnings in Santa Cruz County as Surf Nears 50 Feet
events.summary: Santa Cruz County and Capitola police issued evacuation warnings for low-lying coastal areas from Capitola Village to Aptos ahead of a storm expected to bring 25-35 foot waves, with surf near 50 feet forecast at Mavericks. The city of Santa Cruz closed all beaches and its wharf, with a second storm and swell expected Sunday into Monday.

events.headline: North Carolina Regulators Demand Broader Chemours PFAS Cleanup Plan at Fayetteville Works
events.summary: North Carolina's environmental agency told Chemours its PFAS cleanup plan for the Fayetteville Works site is deficient and must be expanded to test for all PFAS compounds, with a revised plan due within 60 days. The order follows a $590 million settlement in September and roughly $1.2 billion already spent on consent-order compliance.

events.headline: Teacher, Two Students Stabbed at Missouri Middle School; Student Suspect in Custody
events.summary: A student allegedly stabbed two classmates and a teacher at Black Hawk Middle School in Warrenton, Missouri, on the morning of Nov. 12. One student was airlifted in serious condition, the teacher was taken by ambulance in serious condition, and a second student suffered superficial wounds. The suspect, a student, was taken into custody and officials say there is no further public threat.

events.headline: Spain's First General Strike in 14 Years Turns Violent in Barcelona and Madrid
events.summary: More than three million workers joined Spain's first 24-hour general strike since 2012, called over housing costs and prices weeks ahead of an early election; peaceful marches turned violent in Barcelona, with dozens arrested nationwide in clashes with police.

events.headline: St. Johns River Flooding Reaches Major Stage, Threatens Brevard County Homes
events.summary: After up to two feet of rain in two days, the St. Johns River near Cocoa rose to major flood stage, with a crest near 17.1 feet forecast, nearly matching the 2008 Tropical Storm Fay record. Rising water is approaching homes in Rockledge's Silver Pines neighborhood, with flooding expected to persist for weeks.

events.headline: Three Washington School Districts Prepare to Sue State Over Funding Shortfall
events.summary: Lake Washington and Tacoma school boards authorized lawsuit preparation against Washington state in October, joined by Yakima in November, arguing the state again failed its constitutional 'basic education' funding obligation. The shortfall is forcing districts to use local levy dollars for operating costs and has already driven layoffs and larger class sizes, echoing the earlier McCleary case.

events.headline: Bangladesh Garment Factories Shut Down Amid Wage Protests, Threatening Industry-Wide Strike
events.summary: Manufacturers' groups BGMEA and BKMEA threatened an indefinite factory shutdown as wage protests shut 147 garment factories and suspended production at 92 more in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur. Workers are demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka, up from 12,500, and a wage board has agreed in principle to a revised scale effective December.

events.headline: Rare November Tornado Hits Newark, Delaware, Damages Hospital Helicopters
events.summary: A confirmed EF-1 tornado struck near Newark, Delaware, on Nov. 12, knocking a hotel sign onto cars, overturning a tractor-trailer on I-95, and damaging two ChristianaCare medical helicopters at its Newark campus. No injuries were reported in what was only the third November tornado recorded in Delaware since 1950.

events.headline: Wisconsin Gov. Evers Grants First Prison Commutations Since 1995
events.summary: Gov. Tony Evers commuted sentences for 14 of 24 applicants on Nov. 13-14, marking Wisconsin's first commutations in roughly 25 years, including for several people serving life sentences for homicide. The move comes amid record overcrowding in the state's prison system.

events.headline: Vanderbilt University Hit With Second Class-Action Lawsuit Over Cyberattack
events.summary: A ransomware group claimed to have breached Vanderbilt University's systems on Nov. 9, alleging access to over a million Social Security numbers and records, though the university has not independently confirmed the scope. A second class-action lawsuit was filed Nov. 11 alleging inadequate data security, and Vanderbilt has ordered password resets.

events.headline: Central Minnesota Measles Outbreak Grows to About 160 Cases, Largest Since 1990
events.summary: An outbreak centered in Todd County since mid-September has become Minnesota's largest measles year since 1990, with the county accounting for roughly 85% of cases. The statewide total reached about 160 by Nov. 12-13, with most cases among unvaccinated residents and spread confirmed to seven other counties.

events.headline: Audit Finds Choking Death, Operational Failures at North Dakota Veterans Home
events.summary: A state legislative audit found a resident at the North Dakota Veterans Home died after choking because staff did not follow a physician-ordered dietary plan, and that disciplinary records failed to reflect the incident. The audit also flagged over $9.7 million in expenditures approved solely by an administrative assistant and inconsistent overtime logging; findings will be discussed at a Nov. 30 legislative committee meeting.

events.headline: SpaceX Plans $24 Billion Data Center Near Brownsville After Land Deannexed to Bypass City Moratorium
events.summary: SpaceX is planning a $24 billion, 444-acre data center and gas-fired power plant near the Port of Brownsville, Texas, on land the city deannexed at SpaceX's request and then annexed into Starbase, sidestepping a 90-day data-center moratorium the city had just passed. SpaceX pledged $220 million toward water and wastewater infrastructure, but the move has drawn criticism from residents and officials over loss of local control.

events.headline: Delhi Air Quality Crisis Declared 'Public Health Emergency' as AQI Tops 400 Post-Diwali
events.summary: Delhi's air quality plunged to hazardous levels after Diwali firecracker use combined with stagnant weather, with the 24-hour AQI hitting 370-419+ and PM2.5 reaching 993 micrograms per cubic meter in parts of the city. GRAP Stage III emergency measures were invoked across the National Capital Region, affecting over 30 million residents.

events.headline: State Department: US Returned Over $12 Billion in Venezuelan Oil Proceeds Since Maduro's Ouster
events.summary: A State Department report says the US collected $12.26 billion from Venezuelan oil, gold and mineral sales since Maduro's January 2026 ouster, returning about 99% to Venezuelan individuals and businesses, with $168.6 million left in escrow.

events.headline: Brazil's Senate Approves Base Text of Lula's 2027 Fiscal Adjustment Package, Real Stabilizes
events.summary: Brazil's Senate voted 45-31 on November 12 to approve the base text of a fiscal package expected to improve public finances by 45-60 billion reais in 2027. Amendment votes are due November 17.

events.headline: US-Somali Forces Intensify Anti-Al-Shabaab Operations Near Jamaame Amid Famine Warnings
events.summary: AFRICOM conducted an airstrike against al-Shabaab near Jamaame on November 5, its 91st Somalia strike of the year, coinciding with Somali Danab commando ground operations. Somalia faces famine risk after droughts killed over one million livestock.

events.headline: GlobalFoundries Breaks Ground on $10 Billion Chip Fab in Malta, New York
events.summary: GlobalFoundries and Gov. Kathy Hochul marked the Nov. 13 groundbreaking of a $10 billion, 300mm semiconductor fab in Malta as part of a U.S.-Japan chip initiative. The project is expected to create about 1,000 manufacturing jobs and 27,000 construction and ecosystem jobs, with production starting in 2029.

events.headline: JNIM-ISIS Sahel Turf War Spreads to Burkina Faso as State Loses Ground in Oudalan
events.summary: Rivalry between al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and Islamic State-Sahel Province intensified in Burkina Faso, with JNIM encroaching on the Koupela and Pouytenga commercial hubs in Centre-Est and ISSP threatening the Essakane gold mine. Burkinabe state forces are reported to be losing ground in Oudalan province amid the escalating rivalry.

events.headline: Mexican Navy Captures Alleged CJNG Cell Leader Linked to Mayor Manzo's Murder
events.summary: Rafael Alvarez Ayala, alias 'R2', leader of a CJNG cell tied to the murder of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo, was arrested November 8-9 in Zapopan, Jalisco with DEA intelligence support; 20 others were arrested in the related operation.

events.headline: Bus-Truck Collision Near Kaziranga National Park Kills at Least 23 in Assam, India
events.summary: A passenger minibus collided head-on with a container truck on a highway near Kaziranga National Park in Assam, killing at least 23 people including three children; police suspect speeding in a restricted park-area zone caused the driver to lose control.

events.headline: West Virginia Supreme Court Bars 'Deliberate Indifference' Claims in Prison Suits
events.summary: In a 3-2 ruling, West Virginia's Supreme Court held that 'deliberate indifference' is not a cognizable common-law claim, granting writs of prohibition that limit legal recourse for families of inmates who died in custody. The same court separately struck down a 2025 law expanding the legislature's power over the state Board of Education.

events.headline: Record Fentanyl Lab Uncovered in Baton Rouge, Suspect Arrested
events.summary: The East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff's Office uncovered a clandestine fentanyl synthesis lab with professional-grade equipment worth about $250,000, capable of producing roughly 127 pounds of fentanyl powder, enough for nearly 569,000 potentially fatal doses. It is the largest such lab found in the DEA's four-state New Orleans Field Division; Torrey Lewis Jr., 34, was arrested.

events.headline: Montana's GOP Delegation Breaks With Trump Administration Over Public Land Sales
events.summary: The Interior Department's 2026-2030 strategic plan under Secretary Doug Burgum proposes offering public lands for sale or transfer to states, localities and tribes, including for energy production. Montana's entire congressional delegation, including Sens. Tim Sheehy and Steve Daines and Rep. Ryan Zinke, publicly opposed the plan, with Sheehy vowing to block any Montana land sale.

events.headline: Boeing to Cut About 2,500 Commercial Airplanes Jobs in Washington State
events.summary: Boeing announced it will cut about 5%, or roughly 2,500 of 50,000, jobs in its Commercial Airplanes division, citing the need to reset the pace of production ramp-ups amid supply-chain and factory stability issues. The cuts, via attrition and layoffs starting in December, come about a month after the company averted a machinists' strike; the division posted a $697 million quarterly loss despite generating 44% of company revenue.

events.headline: Over 50 Killed as Vigilantes Ambush Bandits Returning From Kidnapping Raid in Zamfara
events.summary: Vigilantes ambushed bandits returning from a kidnapping raid in Gummi district near Zoma village, Bukkuyum local government area of Zamfara State, Nigeria. A village chief said 44 bandits and nine vigilantes were killed in the clash, a toll distinct from a separate civilian massacre reported elsewhere in the state.

events.headline: Salvadoran-Backed Haitian Forces Recapture National Stadium From Gangs in Port-au-Prince
events.summary: Haitian police and armed forces, backed by El Salvador's deployed special forces, recaptured Stade Sylvio Cator, Haiti's national stadium, after roughly two years of gang control; Salvadoran troops have begun using it as a forward operating base. Human skulls were found at the site, pointing to gang atrocities.

events.headline: Leaked Colombian Intelligence Report Alleges Petro-Era Spying on Rivals, Election Meddling
events.summary: A leaked 26-page DNI handover report alleges Colombia's intelligence agency, under the Petro administration, spied on former presidents, infiltrated rival 2026 presidential campaigns under a covert operation, and planned to target the electoral authority's systems. The allegations are unadjudicated and Petro has not responded.

events.headline: China Warns US Against New Chip Export Controls Following Nvidia-Huang Scandal
events.summary: China's Foreign Ministry warned the United States against imposing additional semiconductor export controls, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid allegations tied to a relationship with an executive US intelligence linked to China's Ministry of State Security; the episode comes ahead of an expected Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

events.headline: Armenian Court Orders One-Month Pretrial Detention of Opposition Leader Samvel Karapetyan
events.summary: Karapetyan, a Russian-Armenian billionaire and leader of the 'Strong Armenia' party, was detained November 4 amid an investigation into alleged losses of about $179-180 million at Electric Networks of Armenia. A court ordered one month of pretrial detention; his lawyers call it politically motivated.

events.headline: Georgia's Constitutional Court Continues Hearings on Bid to Ban Five Opposition Parties
events.summary: Georgia's Constitutional Court is hearing a petition by 88 Georgian Dream-aligned lawmakers to ban five opposition entities, alleging they seek to overthrow the constitutional order. Hearings continue to November 17 after two opposition leaders were removed from the courtroom on November 11.

events.headline: Bandits Burn 12 Family Members to Death in Zamfara State Village Attack
events.summary: Suspected bandits attacked Gidan Taba village in Zamfara State on the night of November 7, locking 12 members of a vigilante's family in a room and setting it ablaze, killing all of them. Other residents were kidnapped in an apparent act of retaliation.

events.headline: China's October Exports Jump 35.2%; 10-Month Trade Surplus Tops $1.04 Trillion
events.summary: China's customs data showed October 2026 exports rose 35.2% year-on-year to $412.33 billion, driven by semiconductor and AI-hardware demand. The October trade surplus was $105.3 billion, bringing the January-October cumulative surplus to $1.043 trillion.

events.headline: Indiana Measles Outbreak Tops 160 Cases, Concentrated in LaGrange and Elkhart Counties
events.summary: Indiana's statewide measles case count reached 162 as of Nov. 13, with LaGrange County as the epicenter at 36 confirmed cases, up from 25 the prior week. More than half of all cases are in northeast Indiana, 31 patients have been hospitalized, and most cases involve unvaccinated people under 30, described by officials as the worst outbreak in decades.

events.headline: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins Wins Alaska Governor's Race, Becomes State's First Democratic Governor in Two Decades
events.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former Sitka state legislator, won Alaska's governorship with 50.2% of the vote, clearing the threshold needed to avoid a ranked-choice runoff and defeating Republican Bernadette Wilson and other candidates by a wide margin. He becomes the state's first Democratic governor in about two decades, aided by a cross-party endorsement from Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski.

events.headline: South Sudan Postpones First-Ever National Elections to February 2027
events.summary: South Sudan's National Elections Commission postponed the country's first-ever national elections from December 22, 2026 to February 11, 2027, citing the need for more time on voter registration and logistics. The vote has already been repeatedly delayed since independence in 2011.

events.headline: Turkey and Qatar Sign Mutual Defense Pact
events.summary: Erdogan and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani signed a mutual defense pact in Istanbul pledging a unified response to any external armed attack on either country, part of five agreements reached at the 12th Turkey-Qatar High Strategic Committee meeting.

events.headline: Heaviest Fighting of the Week Hits Pokrovsk Front as Russia Launches Dozens of Assaults
events.summary: Ukraine's military reported 243-273 clashes along the front line on November 13, with up to 47 Russian assault attempts near Dobropillia, Molodetske and Sofiivka in the Pokrovsk sector, the hottest on the front. Shelling of Pokrovsk and Rodynske on November 14 killed one civilian and injured three others.

events.headline: US and Venezuela Discuss Long-Term Troop Presence Agreement After Deadly Apure Drone Strike
events.summary: US officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, confirmed talks on a long-term Status of Forces Agreement for US troops in Venezuela following an October 31 drone strike on an alleged ELN camp in Apure state that killed up to 23 people. Rubio described any formal deal as still 'way, way down the road,' with no agreement finalized.

events.headline: Sudan's RSF Drone Strike Death Toll in Blue Nile Rises to 16 Civilians
events.summary: The civilian death toll from an RSF drone strike on Bani Shako village in Kurmuk county, Blue Nile state, rose from nine to 16. Separately, Sudanese army forces advanced in West Kordofan, pressuring the RSF stronghold of En Nahud after capturing Al-Khuwai and Serif Ankoush.

events.headline: Houthis Claim New Attacks on Saudi Oil Infrastructure; Coalition Reports Interception, No Confirmed Damage
events.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline pumping station, the Yanbu oil facility, and an Aramco site in Riyadh; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones and reported no confirmed facility damage from the claimed attacks.

events.headline: Suicide Car Bombing at Balochistan Security Checkpoint Kills Five
events.summary: A suicide car bomber attacked a Frontier Corps checkpoint on the N-25 highway in Mastung district, Balochistan, killing five (including two civilians and the bomber) and injuring 13; the banned Baloch Liberation Army claimed responsibility.

events.headline: Fourth Round of Venezuela Government-Opposition Talks Opens in Caracas
events.summary: A fourth cycle of US-backed talks between Delcy Rodriguez's government and the opposition, led by Dinorah Figuera, opened November 11 and runs through November 15, focused on new Supreme Court and electoral-council mechanisms and prisoner releases.

events.headline: Russian Overnight Attack Injures Two, Damages Kindergarten and Homes in Vinnytsia
events.summary: A Russian strike early on November 13 injured two women and damaged a kindergarten, homes and apartment buildings in Vinnytsia, Ukraine.

events.headline: Coalition of 53 States Urges Israel's Incoming Government to Expand Gaza Humanitarian Access
events.summary: A joint statement delivered November 12 by the UK's UN ambassador on behalf of 53 states and organizations called on Israel's incoming post-election government to allow rapid humanitarian and medical access to Gaza, citing winter hypothermia and disease risks for displaced Palestinians.

events.headline: Two J&K Special Police Officers Found Shot Dead, Service Weapons Missing, in Kishtwar
events.summary: The bodies of two Special Police Officers, missing since November 10 while moving between an SOG camp and an army post, were recovered on November 12 in a forest near Dachhan, Kishtwar. Their service weapons were missing, raising suspicion of militant involvement.

events.headline: APEC Leaders' Meeting Set for Shenzhen Nov. 18-19 With Trump, Putin, Xi Among Expected Attendees
events.summary: The APEC Leaders' Meeting is scheduled in Shenzhen, China for November 18-19, 2026, chaired by Xi Jinping. Trump, Putin and Philippine President Marcos Jr. are among those expected to attend alongside leaders from Canada, Australia, Mexico, Indonesia and other members, though Putin's in-person attendance is not yet confirmed by tier-1 wire sources.

events.headline: Armenia Says Its CSTO Membership 'Has Run Its Course' as Kremlin Strips Its Voting Rights
events.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said membership in the Russia-led CSTO military alliance 'has run its course,' as the Kremlin confirmed Armenia has been stripped of its voting rights within the bloc. Pashinyan said Armenia aims to submit an EU membership application in 2027 or 2028.

events.headline: Kenya Discharges Last Ebola Patient, Starts 42-Day Countdown to Outbreak-Free Declaration
events.summary: Kenya's last Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) patient, linked to the wider DRC outbreak, was discharged on Nov 11, starting the WHO-standard 42-day countdown toward a possible outbreak-free declaration around Dec 23. Kenya recorded nine cases since early October with two deaths and seven recoveries.

events.headline: Storm Charles Floods French and Italian Riviera as Italy Issues Highest-Level Rain Warning
events.summary: Storm Charles moved northeast from Portugal to flood Nice, Cannes, Mandelieu and Corsica in France with up to 140mm of rain, closing roads and prompting rescues. Italy issued a red rainfall warning from Tuscany to Venice, forecasting up to 200mm more rain.

events.headline: Second Wave of Hoax Bomb Threats Hits Thousands More Italian Schools, Prompts Terrorism Investigation
events.summary: A second wave of hoax bomb-threat emails hit well over a thousand additional Italian schools on Nov 12, after an earlier wave targeted thousands more on Nov 11; Rome anti-terrorism prosecutors opened an investigation, with IP addresses reportedly traced to the Philippines, Taiwan and Australia.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes and Home Demolitions Continue Across Southern Lebanon Despite Framework Deal
events.summary: Israeli forces continued strikes and artillery fire on villages across southern Lebanon, including Khiam, Khraybeh, Mayfadoun and Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh, and demolished homes with explosives despite a framework ceasefire deal. Drones were also reported flying low over Beirut.

events.headline: Israeli Forces Shell Rural Quneitra and Abduct Two Men in Fresh Southern Syria Incursion
events.summary: Israeli forces fired artillery shells into a forested area near Briqa village in rural Quneitra and separately raided homes in Jabata al-Khashab, abducting two young men, in a continuation of near-daily incursion patterns documented across southern Syria.

events.headline: Taiwan Indicts Couple Over Chinese-Origin Chips Found in Military Drones
events.summary: Taichung prosecutors indicted Align Corp. director Tu Ta-sen and his wife, seeking at least five-year sentences, for allegedly supplying Chinese-origin chips in drones under four Taiwanese military procurement contracts that explicitly barred Chinese components; the chips were found in training drones and explosive-dropping drones.

events.headline: Lebanese Army Seizes Large Weapons Cache in Raid on Beirut's Southern Suburbs
events.summary: Lebanese army military intelligence raided a weapons warehouse in the Msharafieh area of Beirut's southern suburbs, a Hezbollah stronghold, seizing rifles, machine guns, rocket and grenade launchers and explosives, and detaining one suspect, as the state pushes to assert control over weapons in the area.

events.headline: 19 Inches of Hail Blankets Delaware County, Pennsylvania Amid Tornado Watch
events.summary: A severe Nov. 12 storm dumped roughly 19 inches of hail in Parkside Borough and Brookhaven, Delaware County, Pennsylvania, burying streets like a snowstorm. A tornado watch and flash flooding also triggered water rescues in nearby Chester Township and Aston; no injuries were reported.

events.headline: Nevada Lawmakers Brace for $1 Billion-Plus Budget Boost Ahead of 2027 Session
events.summary: Forecasters project Nevada's 2027-2029 biennial budget could grow $900 million to $1.64 billion above the current $49.5 billion budget, driven by rising sales and gaming tax revenue. Democratic Sen. Edgar Flores was selected as the new Senate Majority Leader after Democrats expanded their legislative majority in the Nov. 2026 elections; an official forecast is set for approval Nov. 16.

events.headline: Over 100,000 Join Fifth Consecutive Weekend of Nationwide Protests in France
events.summary: France's Interior Ministry counted 106,000 protesters nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris, on the fifth consecutive Saturday of demonstrations, while organizers claimed up to 200,000. About 70,000 police were deployed and 219 people were arrested amid clashes in Nantes, Bordeaux, Lyon and Paris.

events.headline: Tens of Thousands March Across 32 Portuguese Cities Over Housing Crisis
events.summary: Protesters marched in 32 cities across Portugal on November 14 demanding rent caps and stronger tenant protections amid new eviction-timeline legislation. Organizers say the housing crisis has made rents increasingly unaffordable for low- and middle-income residents.

events.headline: Syria Confirms Third Poliovirus Case in Deir ez-Zor, Expands Vaccination Campaign
events.summary: Health authorities confirmed a third case of vaccine-derived poliovirus (VDPV1) in Mayadin, Deir ez-Zor province, Syria, prompting an expanded vaccination response. Lebanon's health ministry held an emergency cross-border readiness meeting in response to the outbreak.

events.headline: EU Forms 'E5' Team of Five Nations for Ukraine Peace Talks, Sidelining Kallas as Lead Negotiator
events.summary: EU leaders agreed to form an 'E5' negotiating team -- the EU plus Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland -- to represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks. Foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas was denied the lead negotiator role, saying 'the Russians do not want me.'

events.headline: Eight-Storey Building Under Construction Collapses Near Nairobi, Killing Six
events.summary: An eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Mombasa Road outside Nairobi while workers were pouring a ninth-floor concrete slab, killing six people; all other workers on site were accounted for. It is the second deadly Nairobi-area building collapse in three weeks.

events.headline: 49th ASEAN Summit Opens in Manila With Philippines-Australia Defense Pact Signed
events.summary: The 49th ASEAN Summit opened in Manila on November 15 for three days of meetings. Philippine Defense Secretary Teodoro and Australian Ambassador Innes-Brown signed an upgraded defense cooperation agreement witnessed by Prime Minister Albanese, while Trump is expected around November 17 for sideline Quad talks.

events.headline: Inter-American Development Bank Approves Country Engagement Note to Resume Venezuela Operations
events.summary: The IDB's board unanimously approved a country engagement note for Venezuela, its first formal roadmap for renewed operations since halting new lending in 2018. The note sets priorities such as electricity-sector rehabilitation and food security but does not clear Venezuela's roughly $2.3 billion in arrears.

events.headline: Biden Says Prostate Cancer Spread to Bones Is 'Slowing Him Down,' Scales Back Book Tour
events.summary: Former President Joe Biden said his stage IV prostate cancer, which has spread to his bones, is slowing him down, prompting him to scale back the promotional tour for his memoir 'Promise Me, America,' due out November 17. He disclosed the update from his home in Wilmington, Delaware.

events.headline: Argentina's Milei Confirms 2027 Re-Election Bid as Economy Slips Into Technical Recession
events.summary: President Javier Milei confirmed he will seek re-election in 2027 even as Argentina's economy entered a technical recession with a second consecutive quarterly contraction. His approval rating has slipped to around 36 percent amid continued austerity measures.

events.headline: Chile Ends Truckers' Strike With Diesel Price Cut Deal, But Kast's Approval Keeps Falling
events.summary: Chile's government reached a deal with truckers on November 12-13 to end a strike that began November 10 over diesel prices, cutting the price by 142 pesos per liter and freezing it through March 2027 at a cost of about $500 million. Some unrest and roadblocks persisted into November 14, as President Kast's approval rating fell to about 24 percent.

events.headline: Japan Confirms Second Bird Flu Outbreak of the Season at Chiba Poultry Farm
events.summary: Japan confirmed its second bird flu outbreak of the season at a poultry farm in Asahi, Chiba Prefecture on November 13, a day after an outbreak in Kameoka, Kyoto led to the culling of 200,000 birds. Chiba will cull about 40,000 egg-laying chickens and has banned transport of 5.62 million birds from 49 farms within 10 kilometers.

events.headline: Suspected Unauthorized Drone Activity Reported Over US-Operated RAF Lakenheath Base in UK
events.summary: US Air Force Security Forces at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity on the evening of Nov 13; no personnel, aircraft, or infrastructure were affected and the situation was resolved. It comes amid heightened security around UK-based US bases tied to Iran-linked threat warnings.

events.headline: Venezuela Deploys Troops to Apure After ELN Kidnaps Colombian Army Officer
events.summary: Venezuela's armed forces deployed military patrols into Apure state after the ELN's Eastern War Front abducted a Colombian army sub-lieutenant near the border. Bogota and Caracas have agreed to coordinate on border security, a notable cooperation shift amid US pressure in the region.

events.headline: EU and UK Warn Kosovo Against Curbing Hague War Crimes Court's Powers
events.summary: The EU Office in Kosovo and the British Embassy in Pristina publicly warned against opposition-driven amendments that would curb the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers' powers, including letting the president pardon convicts, following the court's conviction of ex-PDK leader Hashim Thaci and three co-defendants.

events.headline: Syria's Interior Ministry to Integrate 800 Kurdish YPJ Fighters Into Special Battalions
events.summary: A YPJ spokesperson said Syria's interim government agreed to integrate roughly 800 all-female YPJ fighters into two special battalions under the Interior Ministry, a compromise after the SDF's August dissolution; the Syrian government had not yet formally confirmed the agreement at time of reporting.

events.headline: India's October Retail Inflation Breaches RBI Upper Limit at 6.09%
events.summary: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% year-on-year in October, above the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time since October 2024, driven by food inflation climbing to 8.94% as onion prices surged over 116%.

events.headline: Hong Kong Raises 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to 4.8% on AI-Driven Export Boom
events.summary: Hong Kong's government raised its full-year 2026 real GDP growth forecast to 4.8%, up from a prior 3.5-4.5% range, citing a surge in AI-related electronics exports; Q3 GDP grew 5.2% year-on-year with total goods exports up 30.3% in real terms, the fastest annual growth pace in five years.

events.headline: Bavaria Holds State Funeral for Former Deputy Minister-President Hubert Aiwanger
events.summary: Bavaria held a state funeral for former Deputy Minister-President Hubert Aiwanger at Munich's Frauenkirche on November 14. Aiwanger, who died on November 4 after being found dead in a Berlin hotel room, showed no evidence of third-party involvement in his death.

events.headline: Pakistan to Send Climate Minister to India for SCO Forum, First Ministerial Visit in Three Years
events.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced that Climate Minister Musadik Malik will represent Pakistan at the SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20-22, marking the first Pakistani ministerial visit to India in three years. The visit comes amid a prolonged diplomatic freeze between the two countries.

events.headline: AfD Nominates Former Footballer Thomas Berthold as Candidate for German Federal President
events.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party nominated former national team footballer Thomas Berthold as its candidate for federal president. The nomination is largely symbolic, as the party has no realistic path to winning the largely ceremonial post.
